source.title: StableGrad: Backward Scale Control without Batch Normalization
source.authors: José I. Mestre; Alberto Fernández-Hernández; Cristian Pérez-Corral; Manel Dolz; Enrique S. Quintana-Ortí

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether optimizer-level gradient rescaling enables training in BatchNorm-free CNNs, but uses a different intervention from the claim versions’ initialization, residual shortcut, and batch-normalization comparisons.
record.gate_note: The CNN results bear on V6: StableGrad enables training without BatchNorm and is compared with BatchNorm baselines. PINN and local-dynamics results do not measure a claim version’s named training classification-error outcome. Cited prior-work summaries are not rows. CNN validation accuracies are reported in the text and Figure 2; the figure does not give exact final values beyond the text’s approximate descriptions.
record.test_reason: The matched default-BatchNorm versus BatchNorm-removed controls test V6 in new architecture/dataset settings: BatchNorm models gain accuracy while otherwise matched models collapse. These controls are missing from the rows. StableGrad comparisons alone do not isolate BatchNorm's effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete: the authors primarily present StableGrad for PINNs, reporting improved matched-depth accuracy and more reliable deeper training. CNNs provide a diagnostic demonstration that it prevents collapse after BatchNorm removal. They explicitly acknowledge that it guarantees neither stable raw backpropagated adjoints nor stable forward activations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses optimizer-level layerwise gradient rescaling after backpropagation, with BatchNorm removed from the evaluated CNNs; it does not reproduce the versions’ original interventions or classification training-error measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on architecture and dataset: StableGrad exceeds the BatchNorm baseline on EfficientNetV2-S/CIFAR-100 but falls below it on ResNet-50/ImageNet-1k. Sign-based preprocessing fails in the EfficientNetV2-S/CIFAR-100 BatchNorm-free setting.

fits_no_version.finding: StableGrad enables BatchNorm-free EfficientNetV2-S to exceed 77% validation accuracy and BatchNorm-free ResNet-50 to reach about 67%; sign preprocessing collapses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layerwise gradient rescaling can restore trainability to these BatchNorm-free CNNs under the tested protocols.

record.problems: CNN outcomes are reported as validation accuracy, not training classification error. The text gives approximate accuracy values and no uncertainty estimates. The ResNet result is on ImageNet-1k, outside V6’s stated CIFAR-10 setting.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows identified. PINN benchmark metrics, controlled Burgers diagnostics, and learning-rate scheduler comparisons do not measure the training classification-error behavior specified by the versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, random labels, and effects of model size, stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training error in plain versus residual CNNs; special tanh initialization and Fixup.
Initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable depth. Figure 1 measures initial signal scales, without comparing learning speed or trainable depth across initializations.
Above-threshold loss recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence from below threshold. The PINN effective-kernel diagnostics stay well below their local stability threshold.

Higher learning-rate tolerance, the specified original architecture/dataset settings, and training without normalization using Fixup. StableGrad versus BatchNorm curves do not isolate training-speed differences.

missing.what: Add matched BatchNorm-present and BatchNorm-removed control outcomes for EfficientNetV2-S/CIFAR-100: roughly 75% versus approximately 1% validation accuracy, with the removed-BatchNorm model suffering forward overflow and NaNs before 500 batches. These controls isolate the normalization intervention.
missing.locator: Section 5.1; Figure 2(a) and caption; Appendix C.1; Appendix C.3

missing.what: Add matched BatchNorm-present and BatchNorm-removed control outcomes for ResNet-50/ImageNet-1k: about 71% versus approximately 0% validation accuracy in Figure 2, with almost immediate collapse after BatchNorm removal.
missing.locator: Section 5.1; Figure 2(b) and caption; Appendix C.3

record.verdict_notes: Validation accuracy is relevant to V6's accuracy-gain claim, though it cannot establish V1's training-error claim. ImageNet/ResNet-50 is a new V6 setting, not a reason by itself for a limits_scope verdict. No learning-rate sweep or uncertainty estimates are reported for the CNN comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error from random initialization, including corrupted or random labels; model size, duration and regularization effects.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU spurious minima and student-width effects.
Plain versus residual networks as depth increases, and special initialization or Fixup results.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, propagation stability and depth trainability.
Training above a stability limit, loss recovery or divergence, and sharpness dynamics.

The study tests StableGrad as a way to train BatchNorm-free CNNs against BatchNorm baselines. It does not test adding BatchNorm versus no BatchNorm under an otherwise identical training method to compare speed and learning-rate tolerance; its ImageNet ResNet-50 result is not a CIFAR-10 result.

rows.subject: EfficientNetV2-S
rows.stage_stated: trained for 100 epochs; training method AdamW
rows.baseline: roughly 75% for the default BatchNorm model
rows.note: Authors state StableGrad converges faster than the BatchNorm baseline and reaches higher validation accuracy. The result is described approximately; no uncertainty is given.
rows.check: Reports the proposed method's performance while changing both normalization and gradient processing. The >77% versus roughly 75% comparison does not isolate BatchNorm's effect or test Fixup. The numbers are accurate; Appendix C.3 specifies evaluation using the best validation checkpoint.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.stage_stated: trained for 70 epochs using SGD with momentum 0.9
rows.baseline: about 71% for the default BatchNorm model
rows.note: StableGrad keeps the BatchNorm-free model trainable and near the BatchNorm baseline, but its reported accuracy is lower.
rows.check: Reports the proposed method's performance while changing both normalization and gradient processing. About 67% versus 71% does not establish an incomplete V6 effect: StableGrad is a different intervention from Fixup. The numbers are accurate and use the best validation checkpoint.

rows.subject: EfficientNetV2-S
rows.operation_detail: BatchNorm-free architecture with sign-based gradient preprocessing
rows.baseline: chance level on CIFAR-100, stated as near 1%
rows.value: training collapsed by epoch 2; validation accuracy remained near 1%
rows.note: Comparator/control for StableGrad’s BatchNorm-free training result; the sign-based variant fails to train.
rows.check: The sign-preprocessing control tests a gradient-processing alternative without a matched BatchNorm counterpart. Collapse by epoch 2 and approximately 1% accuracy are correctly reported, but do not measure the effect of adding BatchNorm.

relationships.condition: EfficientNetV2-S on CIFAR-100; matched AdamW protocol with versus without BatchNorm, without StableGrad
relationships.reason: From the text and Figure 2, pending missing rows: BatchNorm reaches roughly 75% validation accuracy; removing it causes early overflow and collapse, with accuracy around 1%.
relationships.display_finding: Batch-normalized training reached roughly 75% validation accuracy, while removing normalization caused early overflow and collapse to around 1%.

relationships.condition: ResNet-50 on ImageNet-1k; matched momentum-SGD protocol with versus without BatchNorm, without StableGrad
relationships.reason: From the text and Figure 2, pending missing rows: BatchNorm reaches about 71% validation accuracy; removing it causes almost immediate collapse, with accuracy plotted around 0%.
relationships.display_finding: Batch-normalized training reached about 71% validation accuracy, while removing normalization caused almost immediate collapse to around 0%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
